title: Scared of the Dip? 16 YouTubers Agree on These 5 Stocks
creator: BWB - Business With Brian
source_note: Detailed summary generated from video captions
summary: Brian distils the dip-buying views of 16 YouTubers after the 5 November sell-off, ranking the five stocks they agree on most, and adds his own calls. He frames the pullback as normal, noting 25 such episodes in 15 years, and argues Wall Street cannot win on capex: spending more is called reckless, spending less is called the end of the AI trade. His anchors first, Neo Clouds last. Meta is his top pick: 8 of 16 bullish, none bearish, sales up 26% with about 15% fewer employees and higher ad prices, though data-centre spending burned through last quarter's cash. Amazon follows on AWS, which has accelerated every quarter from about 17% to close to 40% growth and now makes about 63% of operating profit, though 46% of profit is Anthropic revaluation paper gains. Nvidia, Microsoft, AMD, Micron, Sandisk, Bloom Energy, CoreWeave and Nebius are also ranked. Calls: META BUY (first tracked); AMZN BUY, flipped from CONDITIONAL_BUY; NVDA CONDITIONAL_BUY, flipped from BUY; MSFT HOLD reiterated; AMD HOLD, flipped from BUY; MU HOLD, flipped from SELL/trim; SNDK HOLD, flipped from AVOID; BE HOLD (first tracked); CRWV AVOID for new money (first tracked); NBIS AVOID for new money, flipped from BUY. He holds his own Nvidia shares and has no dry powder, so the conditional buy is for non-owners. Other names discussed include Dan Ives' view that Nvidia's worst case is only 25-30% downside.

calls.video_title: Scared of the Dip? 16 YouTubers Agree on These 5 Stocks
calls.stance_flip: Was SELL (trim) on 8 Nov; now HOLD.
calls.thesis: HOLD - FLIP from SELL (8 Nov trim at all-time highs): memory is a mid-tier holding at a smaller slice, not because a bust is coming - demand is booked far ahead and the cycle looks stretched, not broken; Micron keeps ~81% of sales as operating profit (was ~33% a year ago). His system flags peak earnings, but he disagrees this is the same old cycle.
calls.base_case: HBM demand entrenched, AI/inference growing; memory replaced with every chip generation, forcing repeat buying.
calls.bull_case: Demand runs far ahead of supply with years of bookings; market still views Micron through its legacy lens.
calls.bear_case: Record profits are historically what the top of the cycle looks like; memory stocks swing hard (proved by the -17% day).

calls.base_case: Signed orders harder to walk away from than one-off sales.
calls.bull_case: Storage is essential to AI data centres; reservation book de-risks demand.
calls.bear_case: Memory is boom-and-bust; flash price compression risk was his prior concern.
